title: Hardware fingerprinting and deterministic seeding for stable variant performance profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We observe subtle, repeatable performance deltas across nominally identical SKUs (A100/H100/L40S/MI300) and across cloud partner variants. Existing onboarding relies on full-model benchmark runs that are expensive and noisy, which slows onboarding and causes brittle pin decisions.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight, reproducible 'hardware fingerprint' and deterministic seeding workflow that produces a signed performance profile manifest per (model, hw-variant, runtime-config). The fingerprint + seeded calibration will be used to: (1) automatically select the most compatible variant during onboarding, (2) provide a stable basis for semantic version pinning (soft vs hard pin), and (3) publish a signed profile artifact to the model-catalog for runtime consumption and Console display.

Approach:
- Implement hw-fingerprint CLI (C++/Rust binary called from onboarding pipeline) that runs micro-benchmarks: kernel micro-latency probes, memory-bandwidth probes, KV-cache collision simulation, and small-batch token-generation measurement. The tool outputs a compact fingerprint vector and metadata (driver, cuda/cuDNN versions, BIOS/firmware hints).
- Design a deterministic seeder harness: fixed prompt corpus (seed-set v1) derived from production telemetry buckets; deterministic RNG seeds; warm cache priming steps to populate KV caches. Seeder runs short model-generation calibration (N=20 iterations) to produce per-metric statistics (p50/p95/p99 token-latency, throughput at batch sizes [1,4,8], kv-memory footprint).
- Profile signer: use CI-managed signing key to produce signed profile manifests (schema v2) containing fingerprint, statistical envelopes, quantization flag, runtime kernel hints, and a canonical sample trace. Signed manifests are pushed to model-catalog and attached to the model version.
- Runtime integration: runtime will query catalog, compare node fingerprint to available manifests using a similarity scoring function. If similarity > 0.92 use hard-pin; if 0.80-0.92 use soft-pin with hysteresis and continuous telemetry gating; otherwise fallback to nearest compatible variant.
- Stability gates & telemetry: define gate thresholds for profile acceptance (max allowed variance from canonical p95, jitter thresholds). Use rolling-median noise filter and require stability across 3 independent seed runs before publishing.

Deliverables: hw-fingerprint binary, seeder harness, profile-signer, manifest schema v2, onboarding pipeline changes (GitHub actions), runtime selection change, Console UI additions (display fingerprint match score and signed artifact link), runbook for re-signing/revoking profiles.

Why this is different: Focus is on a fast, deterministic calibration that produces a small artifact (signed manifest) used both by onboarding and the runtime for live selection and safe pinning. This reduces need for full-model lengthy benchmarks for initial decisions and makes pinning decisions repeatable across infra churn.
acceptance_criteria: hw-fingerprint produces a stable vector: mean pairwise distance < 0.03 across 10 cold-start runs on the same host image
seeder harness creates a profile with p95, p99, batch-throughput and kv-footprint; values within 5% of full-benchmark baseline for tracked workloads
signed manifest schema v2 validated by Console and runtime unit tests
runtime correctly selects hard-pin when fingerprint similarity >= 0.92 in 95% of simulated onboarding traffic
CI pipeline auto-creates a catalog PR with artifact and a signed manifest; reviewers can accept or flag candidate for manual review
Runbook for profile revocation and rollback published in Confluence (includes steps to revoke signing key and mark manifest deprecated)
